inventory_scope: Seed records verified against the linked public source during this pass. This is not an exhaustive standards inventory or a claim of Pulse interoperability.

entries.title: Bluetooth Core Specification
region_scope: regional spectrum rules and device certifications apply

evidence.claim: The official Bluetooth Core Specification page identifies version 6.3 and date 2026-05-05; this is source metadata only, not a Pulse conformance result.

entries.notes: Choose only required Bluetooth profiles and OS-exposed capabilities for the target platform. A current Core specification does not imply every controller, profile, or mobile OS exposes the needed functionality.

entries.title: IEEE Standard for Low-Rate Wireless Networks
region_scope: PHYs and permitted operating modes vary by region

relations.notes: The active standard page lists 802.15.4ac-2026 among amendments.
The active standard page lists 802.15.4ae-2026 among amendments.

evidence.claim: IEEE identifies 802.15.4-2024 as active and lists 802.15.4ac-2026 and 802.15.4ae-2026 as amendments.

entries.notes: This record describes PHY/MAC scope only. Thread, Zigbee, Matter, and vendor mesh implementations add distinct layers and profiles; do not treat this entry as evidence that any of them work.

entries.title: IEEE 802.15.4ac-2026 amendment

relations.notes: The IEEE page lists this amendment for the base standard; obtain the amendment's own normative text before implementing it.

entries.notes: The source page confirms the amendment identifier but this seed does not capture its full text, exact publication date, or implementation requirements.

entries.title: IEEE 802.15.4ae-2026 amendment

relations.notes: The IEEE page lists this amendment for the base standard; obtain the amendment's own normative text before implementing it.

entries.notes: The source page confirms the amendment identifier but this seed does not capture its full text, exact publication date, or implementation requirements.

entries.title: LoRaWAN Link Layer Specification package
region_scope: AU915 and other regional variants as defined by the applicable profile

evidence.claim: The official LoRa Alliance page identifies a LoRaWAN 1.0.4 package including link-layer specification, certification protocol, certification requirements, and a reference implementation validated for named regions.

entries.notes: This is not a LoRa PHY implementation record. The LoRa radio technology, LoRaWAN protocols, network-server APIs, certification tools, and regional parameters must be tracked distinctly.

entries.title: LoRaWAN TS014 device-profile onboarding specification

evidence.claim: LoRa Alliance's 2026-08-04 announcement says TS014 enables LoRaWAN networks to automatically pull device profiles; the normative spec, edition, and applicability still need direct review.

entries.notes: Announcement is a discovery pointer rather than the normative specification. This concerns provisioning, not Pulse message transport itself.

entries.title: LoRaWAN TS018 device-profile QR provisioning specification

evidence.claim: LoRa Alliance's 2026-08-04 announcement says TS018 uses the device identification QR code to encode the device profile server; the normative spec, edition, and applicability still need direct review.

entries.notes: Announcement is a discovery pointer rather than the normative specification. This concerns provisioning, not Pulse message transport itself.

entries.title: LoRaWAN TR016 relay implementation guidance

evidence.claim: LoRa Alliance's 2026-08-04 announcement describes TR016 as technical guidance for interoperable LoRaWAN Relay products; the normative document and applicability still need direct review.

entries.notes: Announcement is a discovery pointer rather than the normative report. Review the target relay architecture before any Pulse adapter decision.

entries.title: Bundle Protocol Version 7

relations.notes: RFC Editor lists RFC 9713 as updating RFC 9171.
RFC Editor lists RFC 9758 as updating RFC 9171.

evidence.claim: RFC Editor describes BPv7 as a store-carry-forward overlay suitable for intermittent connectivity and lists RFC 9713 and RFC 9758 as updates.

entries.notes: Strong architectural candidate for outage-tolerant messaging, but Pulse has not thereby implemented BPv7 or any convergence-layer adapter. RFC status does not imply deployed interoperability.

entries.title: Bundle Protocol Security (BPSec)

relations.notes: BPSec specifies security services for Bundle Protocol bundles.

evidence.claim: RFC Editor identifies RFC 9172 as an Internet Standards Track Proposed Standard defining integrity and confidentiality services for BP bundles; errata must be reviewed before adopting a profile.

entries.notes: The RFC Editor errata page showed reported errata during this review. Track reported versus verified errata distinctly and assess impact on the exact profile being implemented.

entries.title: Bundle Protocol Version 7 Administrative Record Types Registry

relations.notes: Clarifies use of the IANA Bundle Administrative Record Types registry for BPv7.

evidence.claim: RFC Editor says RFC 9713 updates RFC 9171 and was published January 2025.

entries.notes: Read together with BPv7 and the relevant IANA registry. This seed does not record application implementation support.

entries.title: Updates to the 'ipn' URI Scheme

relations.notes: Updates encoding and decoding of 'ipn' URIs when used as BPv7 endpoint identifiers.

evidence.claim: RFC Editor says RFC 9758 updates RFC 9171 and was published May 2025.

entries.notes: Endpoint identifier normalization must follow the normative update. Do not treat different encoded representations as different logical endpoints if the standard defines them as equivalent.

entries.title: Default Security Contexts for Bundle Protocol Security (BPSec)

relations.notes: Defines default integrity and confidentiality security contexts for BPSec blocks.

evidence.claim: RFC Editor describes the document as defining default integrity and confidentiality security contexts for BPSec. This is a source reference, not a Pulse implementation or cryptographic approval.

entries.notes: BPSec block-level security and Pulse's existing end-to-end message cryptography are different layers. Do not replace or weaken Pulse V2 based on this registry entry.

entries.title: Delay-Tolerant Networking TCP Convergence-Layer Protocol Version 4 (TCPCLv4)

relations.notes: TCPCLv4 transports BPv7 bundles over TCP and acts as a convergence-layer protocol; it is not a routing algorithm.

evidence.claim: RFC Editor describes TCPCLv4 as a reliable TCP convergence layer for BPv7 bundles with security and extensibility mechanisms.

entries.notes: This is a useful reference for separating store-and-forward semantics from a link-specific convergence layer. It does not by itself qualify TCPCL on any Pulse deployment.

entries.title: Delay-Tolerant Networking Architecture

relations.notes: Foundational DTN architecture; consult the current BPv7 RFCs for normative wire-protocol details.

evidence.claim: RFC Editor catalogue identifies RFC 4838 as the Delay-Tolerant Networking Architecture. It is architectural background, not a transport implementation.

entries.notes: Useful for the delivery model and challenged-network threat assumptions; BPv7 and the chosen convergence layer define the implementation details.

entries.title: Briar offline and online synchronization architecture (implementation reference)

evidence.claim: Briar documentation describes synchronization via Bluetooth or Wi-Fi when offline and via Tor when online, with contact- and share-scope-dependent synchronization semantics.

entries.notes: Use as a design comparison for consent-scoped offline synchronization and battery/network controls. It is not a standards document or evidence of Pulse compatibility.

entries.title: Reticulum medium-agnostic network stack (implementation reference)

evidence.claim: Reticulum's documentation describes a medium-agnostic stack intended for use across diverse digital data links, including radio and serial interfaces. This is a project claim, not independent qualification.

entries.notes: Study its interface abstraction and low-bandwidth design goals; avoid assuming protocol compatibility, cryptographic equivalence, or hardware support. Prefer interop experiments and threat-model comparison before writing a replacement.
